subject: Network segmentation & residency decisions — follow-up and demo plan
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@medivue.com>, Rajesh Iyer <rajesh.iy@medivue.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Network segmentation & residency decisions — follow-up and demo plan

Hi Elena / Rajesh — thanks for a focused conversation today. Quick recap from my side and a proposed next step so we keep momentum.

Key goals you stated:
- Keep all PHI and derived embeddings in-region (US) and stored in customer-managed storage.
- Prevent runtime egress except to a handful of vendor endpoints (no open internet access for inference nodes).
- Support an air-gapped or heavily restricted VPC deployment for certain workloads on day one.
- Maintain sub-300ms median inference latency for the demo workload and predictable unit economics.

Primary constraints we captured:
- No public IPs on inference hosts; all management via bastion/jumpbox controlled by your ops team.
- Outbound allowlist only to: redwood-signer.redwood.ai:443 (updates), s3-us-medivue-upload:443 (model ingest), and our telemetry ingest endpoint (read-only, optional).
- KMS/HSM integration required for key material; retention policy and key rotation owned by Medivue.
- Procurement will require SOC2 evidence and an initial TCO estimate before vendor approval.
- On-prem patching model: models and runtime images must be importable via an offline bundle if air-gapped.

Attachments I've added: network-topology.png (sketch of what we discussed), SOC2-questions.pdf (list of docs we can provide), proposed-demo-agenda.md (30 min).

Proposed next steps (goal: pilot signoff window in Q3):
1) You share a network diagram (VPC CIDRs, NAT/Bastion, DNS/resolver, proxy egress points) to the Drive link below.
2) Security / infra sends a short allowlist for any internal-only endpoints we should expect.
3) Redwood will set up a 30-minute private-demo focused on the Private Console, offline bundle flow, and connection patterns (we'll show HSM/KMS integration patterns).
4) We will provide a ballpark TCO + SOW outline within 3 business days after we have the network diagram.

Calendar options for the demo: June 28 10:00–10:30 PT, June 29 14:00–14:30 PT. If neither work, propose 1–2 slots and we'll adapt.

Drive link to drop the diagram: https://drive.redwood.com/s/medivue-kickoff
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/9876543

Thanks again — looping Ben (dedicated/private lead) and Grace (security lead) so they're aware.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Thanks Jonas — this matches our notes. A couple clarifications from our side:
- For the "air-gapped" ask: some of our clinical customers will require a fully isolated environment (no outbound egress at all). We need to understand how Redwood supports offline model patching and image imports in that scenario.
- Procurement will want a clear SOW + per-month committed-cost (and one-time setup) before legal engages. Can you include a ballpark range in your TCO?
- We're available for the demo the week of June 28; prefer June 29 afternoon PT.

I'll get our infra diagram uploaded to the Drive by EOD Wednesday (June 23). Please include our security lead (procurement@medivue.com is copied) on any compliance artifacts.
